title: CZ stones in silver jewellery: how to keep them sparkling
description: Why CZ stones in silver jewellery go cloudy, a simple cleaning routine to bring back the sparkle, how to check settings, and what to avoid with CZ pieces.
intro: CZ stones lose their sparkle mainly because a thin film of skin oil, soap and lotion builds up on the back of the stone, where light should enter. A soak in warm water with a drop of mild soap and a gentle brush behind the stone usually brings the shine straight back. The silver around it needs its own, separate care.

sections.heading: What CZ actually is
paragraphs: CZ stands for cubic zirconia, a lab-made crystal designed to look like diamond. In India it is also widely sold as American Diamond or AD. It is hard enough to resist everyday scratches better than glass, which is why it is so popular in silver pendants, rings and earrings.

CZ is not as hard as diamond, though, and over years of wear, the facet edges can get tiny nicks if the stone is knocked against harder surfaces. Treating it a little gently keeps it crisp for longer.

sections.heading: Why your CZ looks cloudy
paragraphs: Before deciding a stone is damaged, run through the usual causes. Most of them are fixable at home.
list: Oily film: body lotion, sunscreen, hand cream and natural skin oils coat the stone and blunt its sparkle.
Soap residue: wearing jewellery in the shower leaves a dull layer, especially with hard water.
Trapped dirt: dust collects behind the stone in the setting, blocking light.
Tarnish on the silver: dark metal around a stone makes the stone itself look duller.
Surface scratches: after years of daily wear, fine scratches can genuinely cloud the stone. These cannot be cleaned away.

sections.heading: A five-minute cleaning routine
paragraphs: Fill a small bowl with warm, not hot, water and add a drop or two of a mild dish soap. Soak the piece for about ten minutes to loosen oil and grime.

Using a soft baby toothbrush, brush gently around and behind each stone. The underside matters most, because that is where light enters and bounces back out. Rinse under running water with the sink plug in. Dry with a lint-free cloth, then let it air-dry fully before storing.
If the silver is tarnished, finish with a silver polishing cloth on the metal only. Avoid rubbing the compound into the stone, as it can leave a residue around the setting.

sections.heading: Check the setting while you clean
paragraphs: Cleaning time is a good moment to make sure the stone is secure. Hold the piece close to your ear and give it a gentle shake. A rattle or a faint click can mean a stone is loose. Look at the claws, also called prongs, from the side. They should sit snugly over the edge of the stone, not lifted or bent.

If you see a lifted claw, stop wearing the piece until a jeweller tightens it. It is a quick job, and far cheaper than replacing a lost stone. Also notice whether stones are claw set or glued in. Glued stones should not be soaked for long, as water and heat can weaken the glue.

sections.heading: What not to do with CZ silver jewellery
paragraphs: A few common shortcuts cause more harm than they fix. Skip toothpaste, which is mildly abrasive. Avoid harsh chemical dips and bleach, which can affect the silver and any plating. Do not use ultrasonic cleaners on pieces with glued stones, delicate settings or plating. And never boil jewellery, which risks loosening stones and damaging finishes.
Be careful with the foil and baking soda method too. It is fine for plain sterling with claw-set CZ, but not for gold plated or rhodium plated pieces, where it can affect the finish.

sections.heading: Daily habits that keep the sparkle longer
paragraphs: Put CZ jewellery on after lotion, makeup and perfume. Take it off before bathing, washing dishes, cooking and going to the gym. Wipe it with a soft cloth when you take it off, and store it separately so harder stones and metal do not scratch it.

The same habits apply to CZ and AD necklace sets, though those are often plated brass rather than silver, so they need even gentler cleaning: a soft dry cloth and no soaking. If you own pieces from Varaha's [Heritage American Diamond sets](/heritage) as well as a [925 silver CZ pendant](/silver), clean them separately, using the method that suits each metal.

faq.q: Does CZ lose its sparkle over time?
faq.a: Usually it is buildup rather than the stone itself. A soapy soak and soft brush restores it. Years of heavy wear can scratch the surface slightly.

faq.q: Can I wash CZ silver jewellery with water?
faq.a: Yes, for claw-set stones in sterling silver. Use lukewarm water and mild soap, then dry fully. Avoid soaking glued stones.

faq.q: Is CZ the same as American Diamond?
faq.a: Yes. In India, American Diamond or AD is a common trade name for cubic zirconia.

faq.q: How do I know if a CZ stone is loose?
faq.a: Shake the piece gently near your ear and look at the claws from the side. A rattle or lifted claw means it needs tightening.
